recipes.name: Potato and Cheddar Soup
ingredients_raw: 2 cups peeled and cubed red potatoes

steps.text: Using a medium sized stock pot bring water to a boil, add potatoes and cook until tender. Drain reserving 1 cup liquid.
Stir in butter, onion and flour. Season with salt and pepper. Gradually stir in potatoes, reserved liquid, milk, sugar, cheese, and ham. Simmer for 30 minutes, stirring frequently.

raw_recipe.headline: Potato and Cheddar Soup
raw_recipe.description: This is a smooth creamy soup. Great for those cold winter days.

review.reviewBody: Simple to make. Nice, creamy consistency. But, as a previous reviewer mentioned, the onions are still crunchy after 30 minutes simmer time (I even cooked them in the flour and butter for a couple minutes before adding the rest of the ingredients). I'd highly recommend cooking the onions in the butter first, until soft, then mixing in the flour, etc.

I made this using the recipe as a guideline. I cooked the onions in butter first until soft. Then added everything else. I pulsed it with my hand blender a few times to break up the potatoes and thicken it. I also seasoned it with Adobo, salt, paprika, pepper and a dash of cayenne. I added a cup of chicken broth and some roasted garlic too. It’s a good soup if you’re comfortable self seasoning.

Like other reviewers, I sauteed the butter and onions until the onions were tender and then added the flour. I used 4 slices of cheddar plus 1 cup shredded monteray jack cheese and also used crumbled bacon instead of ham. And added 1 tsp of chicken bouillon granules. I decided against mashing any of the potatoes and I like it this way better (with more chunks). This soup is on par with the best potato soups I've had.

This makes for a great base. I cooked the onions in the butter until they were clear, I also added a half inch sprig of finely chopped garden rosemary and 1 tsp chopped garlic in the onion sautée. I also added 2 more cups of cheese. I used cheddar/jack. 
Instead of the water, I used chicken broth. 
I guess I changed a lot of things, but it came out great.

This was a very yummy soup, but I felt that it was lacking something I couldn't quite put my finger on - that is why I gave it 4 stars. I did sautee the onions in the butter with a little garlic until soft as other reviewers suggested, then added the flour and cooked out the raw flavor of it for a minute, before adding it to the milk, potatoes and other ingredients. I also doubled the cheese and skipped the sugar. It was quite tasty.

I thought this recipe was a great base. I did add a few twists. Thank you to the other reviews. They were very helpful. First I sauteed my onions so they weren't too crunchy and I find sauteeing adds a nice flavor to the onion. I sauteed the onions in bacon fat from bacon cooked to replace the ham. I thought the crunch would really compliment the softness of the potato. I boiled the potatoes (sliced scallop style not chunked) in chicken broth instead of water, aldente. I didn't use red potato. I used a white potato that was in my pantry, which worked just fine. When putting everything together I added corn and extra cheddar. I also added a small bay leaf & some cayenne pepper for bite. I did not add the potatoes to everything until the end so I didn't hurt their shape when stirring the soup. After I added the potatoes I finished cooking them just a bit with a low simmer for about 10 minutes. Like I said, this recipe was a great base but definitely needed added flavor. When I was done I really enjoyed the soup and definitely will make again!

This is a good starter recipe for potato cheddar soup. As mentioned by several reviewers it definitely needs a few extras to improve the flavor which would otherwise be very bland. I have a few tips that made the soup very tasty. I always start my potato soups with mashed potatoes; it gives the soup a nice thick texture. I used crisp bacon, 2 cups of sliced carrots as well as the water I had used to boil them, about a half cup sauteed onions, a tablespoon of chicken broth, and a teaspoon of parsley. With plenty of soup making experience now, I also have a tip regarding the cheese. I put the soup on a low heat to let the flavors blend and at that time sprinkled a few tablespoons of the cheese at a time to give it a chance to melt in. Once it's melted in, give it a stir and add a few more tablespoons until it's all added (as a novice soup maker, I made the mistake of sprinkling all of the cheese in at once and ended up with one lumpy mess of a soup; the cheese all clumped together and ended up very gummy, it was terrible).

Took what folks said about the onions to heart, so I sautéed them with the diced ham. Worked great! Really gave the soup a ton of flavor. I doubled the recipe except for the milk and the flour. I used 4 cups of milk and 3 tbsp of flour, the texture and consistency were perfect. I threw in some extra cheese too (used sharp cheddar), so good!

It was actually quite tasty! I decided to sauté the onions a bit first as I read other comments that they were still kind of raw in theirs. Also instead of ham, I baked some bacon in the oven and crumbled it. And I added it as it was served instead of mixed in. All in all, simple and delicious recipe.

This is absolutely delicious!!! I tweaked the recipe just a tad by adding a few chicken bouillon cubes to the water when boiling the potatoes and therefore using a up of that chicken "broth" to the soup instead of plain water. I also added one diced carrot and used 1 1/2 cups of cheese instead of one cup. My hubby loved it too, I will definitely be making it again. Just a heads up though, it definitely doesn't make 10 servings. My hubby and I both had a large soup mug full and there's enough for maybe 2 more. It's perfect for the 2 of us but just wanted to put that out there for those of you expecting it to make 10 servings.
Husband loved this soup. Substituted chicken broth for water, and used garlic salt instead of regular. Sauteed onions before adding them to the pot and stirring regularly at the end was key.
Loved it! My family could eat it for days if i let them and all our friends love it also. Only thing I changed was I added more ham, potatoes, and cheese due to my family are big eaters.

I used 5 sausage diced, instead of 1 cup ham. Added 16oz chedder, extra potatoes and broccoli florets. I puréed the onion instead of diced. Very filling and absolutely delicious !!!! My husband just loved it! Thank you

I read the reviews carefully before starting this and decided to cook the onions in the butter before adding the flour. It needs that. I left my skins on the potatoes because that is the beauty for me when it comes to red potatoes. No peeling. I really thought this would end up needing herbs or something but it didn't. It was plenty flavorful as is. I'd add more potatoes and cheese next time but overall good as written.

I followed this recipe, but felt that the steps weren't that clear to me. Anyway this came out so darn good, everybody loved it. I added some garlic powder, paprika, garlic oil (I love garlic) and more spices. This came out so good!! I will recommend to sauté the onions with the butter for a while, before you add everything else.
It was delicious!!! Always a hit! This is now a regular in our house. I do cook the onions in the butter first.

I added about a cup more potatoes, and a cup more cheese. 
It's creamy and delicious!
Really great soup. You just need to add your own spices to your liking. I’ve made this 4 times now and it’s been a hit every time. :)
Love it.Yes I put more potatoes and instead ham I did broccoli it is delicious thank you!!!
Double the recipe. It’s better the next day. Didn’t add sugar and didn’t peel the potatoes.
